text:
ops-oncall: observed sustained GPU pool saturation in eu-west2 over the last 6m, autoscaler failing to provision new nodes, ~35% of queued pods in Pending. seeing OOM evictions on some inference pods :frowning: 
raj (infra): grabbing logs now. any recent cluster autoscaler change?
ops-oncall: no config rollouts in the last 12h. autoscaler metrics show provisioning requests spiking and then timing out at the cloud layer (cloud provider returning 502 on create).
emma (sre): confirmed. metric: gce_node_create_errors elevated, median provision latency > 4m. KV: region-wide image-pull latency also higher.
raj (infra): quick mitigation: can we shift non-SLA traffic to eu-west3, and failover warm pools to handle burst?
ops-oncall: yes we have warm pools in eu-west3 and us-west1. recommend shifting 25% traffic to eu-west3 immediately, then scale dedicated burst to 40% if needed.
mike (support): preparing a customer-facing status snippet. draft: "We are experiencing provisioning delays in eu-west2 affecting GPU-backed endpoints. We are migrating traffic and expect partial restoration within 30-45 minutes. Updates every 15 minutes." ok to post?
emma (sre): post with note about impacted features (long-running inference and large-batch endpoints). add a line: "If you rely on reserved Dedicated capacity, reach out to your CSM."
ops-oncall: executing traffic-shift playbook now. running command: ```kubectl label namespace batch shift-failover=eu-west3 --overwrite``` and updating LB weights via terraform apply.
deploy-bot: terraform plan finished, applying weight changes to route table (eu-west2:70 -> eu-west2:50, eu-west3:30, us-west1:20).
ops-oncall: weight changes in progress, routing API returning 202s for some requests but updates accepted.
raj (infra): enabling temporary burst nodes (on-demand) in eu-west3 to absorb queued pods. cost note: expected +$3-4k/hr while burst active.
mike (support): posted status page update and tagged affected customers. link: https://status.redwood.ai/incident/1931009876 — added contact details.
emma (sre): monitoring pod drain times and queue length. current queued pods down from 120 -> 45 after shifting and burst start.
ops-oncall: seeing successful node creates in eu-west3 now, queued pods decreasing. ETA for full recovery ~25m but will update.
mike (support): triage team on standby for escalations; if customer wants immediate SLA-safe migration, advise dedicated failover guide.
raj (infra): follow-up action: open a cloud provider ticket for the create-timeout root cause and add autoscaler circuit-breaker to avoid hitting region-wide provider limits.
emma (sre): noted. will create postmortem runbook and assign action owners once incident stabilizes.
ops-oncall: thanks all — I'll keep updating every 10 minutes. :thumbsup:
